title: Socializing
goal: Join a social conversation, discover a connection, follow up on an answer, and leave or change the topic when you want.

runs.text: Use a brief Chapter 1 greeting or Chapter 2 introduction when needed. Here the next step is making contact beyond the greeting.
Mind if I join you?
Ask to join a person or group.
How do you know Mara?
Ask about a shared host or contact.
Have you been here before?
Ask about experience with the place.
What have you been up to?
Ask about recent activities when reconnecting.
At a friend's gathering

runs.text: The follow-up uses something Robin just said. It gives Robin a clear way to continue instead of introducing an unrelated question immediately.
At a social event,
What do you do?
can ask about someone's work. If you want to be clearer, use
What kind of work do you do?
A person can also explain study, retirement or another current situation.
I work at a library.
Identify your workplace.
I'm studying design.
Describe what you study.
I'm between jobs right now.
Say you are not currently in a job.
I'm retired.
Describe retirement.
We used to work together.
Describe a past connection.
A shared college

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: I went to Westbrook College.

turns.en: I went to Westbrook College.

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: Really? So did I. When were you there?

turns.en: Really? So did I. When were you there?

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: From 2018 to 2022.

turns.en: From 2018 to 2022.

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: I started in 2020. We were there at the same time.

turns.en: I started in 2020. We were there at the same time.

blocks.caption: Work, study, and shared experience · Kai & Robin

runs.text: Westbrook is invented for this scene.
So did I
means Robin also attended. The dates make the overlap clear. If you missed the name,
Could you say the name again?
supplies Chapter 4 repair.

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: I didn't know you were coming! What have you been up to?

turns.en: I didn't know you were coming! What have you been up to?

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: I've been taking a cooking class. How about you?

turns.en: I've been taking a cooking class. How about you?

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: Mostly work, but I started hiking again.

turns.en: Mostly work, but I started hiking again.

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: That sounds fun.

turns.en: That sounds fun.

blocks.caption: Reconnect or make a comment · Robin & Kai

runs.text: The question is about recent activity, so an answer can mention a class, work, a trip or little change:
Not much, mostly work
. You do not need a dramatic story.
A specific compliment can also open a topic:

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: I like your jacket.

turns.en: I like your jacket.

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: Thanks. I found it at a thrift store.

turns.en: Thanks. I found it at a thrift store.

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: Nice find!

turns.en: Nice find!

blocks.caption: Reconnect or make a comment · Kai & Robin

runs.text: A
thrift store
sells secondhand goods. Robin could give only
Thanks
if they did not want to explain where the jacket came from. A compliment does not require a price or shopping story.

study.title: Keep the conversation comfortable for your role

runs.text: I'd rather not talk about work tonight
can change a topic.
What do you do for fun?
asks about interests.
I'm going to get a drink. Good talking with you
can end the exchange; Chapter 10 gives other closing support.
If someone gives a short or private answer, use it rather than demand details:

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: How's work going?

turns.en: How's work going?

turns.speaker: Kai

runs.text: I'd rather not talk about it tonight.

turns.en: I'd rather not talk about it tonight.

turns.speaker: Robin

runs.text: Sure. Have you done any cooking lately?

turns.en: Sure. Have you done any cooking lately?

blocks.caption: Keep the conversation comfortable for your role · Robin & Kai

runs.text: Use these fictional guest cards. Speak both roles when practicing alone.

rows.text: Works with Mara; works at a library; recently started hiking
Took a cooking class with Mara; studies design; likes making bread
Took a photography class with Mara; has been busy with work

runs.text: You are Robin. Join Avery, introduce yourself briefly, and ask how Avery knows Mara. Follow up on work or hiking.
You are Devon. Answer
What do you do?
using the study information. Supply the other person's acknowledgment:
Oh, nice. What kind of design?
For this scene, answer
Graphic design
Reconnect with Avery and ask about recent activities. Avery mentions hiking. Ask
Where do you like to hike?
Avery's supplied answer is
At the nearby park
Change the response: Avery does not want to discuss work. Acknowledge it and ask about hiking instead.
Hide the cards. Build a five-turn conversation from one shared connection. Close it when your role wants to leave.
Sample possibilities
Mind if I join you? — Sure. — I'm Robin. How do you know Mara? — We work together. — What kind of work do you do?
I'm studying design. — What kind? — Graphic design.
What have you been up to? — I started hiking. — Where do you like to hike? — At the nearby park.
Sure. How's the hiking going?
Check:
Did the follow-up connect to an answer? Did each person have room to contribute? Could you respect a topic change and close without making an unwanted promise?
